opening_message:
Ticket 1: Belinda Fuentes (employee ID E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E039.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Admin is only allowed if the employee's role owns the system; Analyst does not own Payroll, so the maximum is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a contractor with basic security training per Security DB (note lists Analyst role). Contractors without advanced training max out at read, never admin. Admin requested exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Belinda Fuentes (E039), an Analyst, requests admin access to Payroll. Per HR's note, she is a full-time employee, so the maximum is write (admin is only allowed if the employee's role owns the system; Analyst does not own Payroll). The Security note lists her as a contractor with basic training, but employment type is an HR fact; HR's database lookup is authoritative. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (write), I grant the maximum: write. I grant no more than requested.

The policy: full-time employees up to write, admin only if role owns system (Analyst doesn't own Payroll, so max write). Contractors: read, or write if advanced security training; never admin.

Either way, requested admin is above maximum. So max is write (if full-time) or read (if contractor). The recommended levels differ: write vs read.
